argv: built in tend deletion 1: below 340 px a walk delete's confirm stacks its actions, the confirm on top and Cancel beneath

ops.body:
**Nov 18, `/tend deletion --deploy=main`, the walk delete confirm at 320 px** (opened from `c9158393`; no sweep, lenses 1-7 not run; aimed at the Deletion section's one `[loop]` item, a medium; the faster lane of decision 0181).
- The rule it broke: `.claude/rules/ui-patterns.md`, "Nothing wraps on a 320 px phone at the default text size": at 320 px the confirm's row gave "Delete walk" 88 px and it wrapped, "Delete / walk". `docs/research/adjacent-apps.md` records no app's two-action alert; the shape follows the platforms' own alerts, which stack two actions that do not fit in a row: HIG Alerts, "In general, place the button people are most likely to choose on the trailing side in a row of buttons or at the top in a stack of buttons. Always place the default button on the trailing side of a row or at the top of a stack. Cancel buttons are typically on the leading side of a row or at the bottom of a stack." (https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/alerts, read Nov 18; not yet recorded in `docs/research/ui-references.md` A2, the review's U4); Material dialogs, "Confirming actions appear above dismissive actions" (A2).
- `tend deletion 1`: below 340 px a walk delete's confirm stacks its actions, "Delete walk" (or "Remove") on top and Cancel beneath, both full width (`confirmActions` in `deletion/core.ts`, `ConfirmCard`); from 340 px the row stays, Cancel leading. No words change. The `deletion` journey measures "Delete walk" on one line and both actions at least 44 px at 390 (154 by 48) and 320 (248 by 48).
- The review (one round, the `ux-reviewer`; four low, the order judged right on both platforms; two accepted, two deferred, none rejected): `tend deletion audit 3` (the switch point measured at 340 and 352 px, where the row holds "Delete walk" on one line, so the threshold stays 340) and `audit 4` (stacked, the two actions 12 px apart, iOS's padding round a bezel; the row keeps 8), in one commit. U3 filed `[owner]` low (the destructive button's filled red in every confirm, a cross-screen call); U4, the HIG Alerts quote above, left for `docs/research/` outside the loop. A line added to `deletion.md`.
- Filed: `[owner]` low, U3, under Deletion. The item built left DEFERRED.
- Journeys on the final export: `deletion` (tend deletion 1, audits 3 and 4), `launch`; typecheck, lint, `npm test`. `tend explore audit 23` (the `memories` journey, which `deletion` runs first) failed on three of four runs, the unchanged base among them, and passed on one: not this run's, left to the explore run. Not run: the sweep's lenses and the balance's evolve. Nothing here has run on a phone: the stacked confirm is drawn by the same views on iOS and Android.

- [owner] The destructive button is a filled red slab in every confirm (a walk's "Delete walk" and "Remove", `ConfirmCard`) and in the three "Discard these edits?" asks (`WalkActions.tsx`, `replay/[id].tsx`, `edit/MediaEditor.tsx`), heavier than either platform draws it: iOS gives the destructive item red text on a plain row with Cancel in bold, Material two text buttons of equal weight that let the words do the work (the reviewer's precedent, not yet recorded in `docs/research/`). Rests on `docs/research/ui-references.md` B3 ("Don't assign the primary role to a button that performs a destructive action") and its goal-to-control matrix, row 8 (Avoid: "a destructive default or primary button"). Stacked at 320 px since `tend deletion 1` it is the first and most saturated thing in the card. A cross-screen call: red text with a red outline and Cancel the stronger style, in every confirm at once so they stay alike (the `tend deletion 1` review's ux U3, Nov 18, low; there before this run)
